newsitem.title: UK: Allied Carpets like-for-like sales up 13pct.
newsitem.headline: Allied Carpets like-for-like sales up 13pct.

text.p: British carpet retailer Allied Carpets Group Plc said on Monday like-for-like sales rose 13 percent in the 26 weeks to December 28, 1996.
The company said it had opened 16 stores in the first half of the year and now had 221 trading.
'I am pleased to announce a satisfactory half year result for our first interim result as a public company,' chairman Julian Lee said in a statement.
Allied Carpets, which floated in July 1996, reported pre-tax profit of 9.03 million pounds in the 26 weeks to December 28, a 24 percent increase.

'Our strategy of meeting customer needs through a wide choice of product, quality and value, together with excellence in service, is moving the business forward. We are in a strong posiiton to increase shareholder value further as consumer confidence returns,' Lee added.
Allied said the carpet market was currently showing growth running at six percent per annum.
The company said it had received 5.6 million pounds from the UK Customs and Excise after the end of the half-year period, following a Court of Appeal ruling.
However, it does not intend to reflect any benefit from this in reported profits until the outcome of an appeal by Customs and Excise to the House of Lords is known.
